title: Having no embedded associated prime is equivalent to Serre's condition S one
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a finite module over a Noetherian ring has no embedded associated prime exactly when it satisfies Serre's condition S one (statement lines 44113-44122). The proof does not invoke a general Cohen-Macaulay criterion: it shows that an embedded associated prime forces the localised support to have dimension at least one, and conversely that positive-dimensional localised support produces an associated prime strictly inside the given one by the correspondence between minimal primes of the support and associated primes (proof lines 44124-44149). Identifying the dimension of the localised support as the precise obstruction is the content. H2.
